title: The WPA band: first trombones, growth to 167 men, and its decline
summary: He names the first 18 men and fellow trombonists, describes Martinez weeding out non-readers, the music-week parade, and why he left as the band shrank.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Do you remember any other trombonists? Dooson you say?
Frankie Dooson and I were the first two trombones in the band.
Was Carnish in there? Do you remember? No, no. Bill Carnish never did get in the band.

Or Sonny Henry? Sonny Henry came in after the band had been organized. Oh, maybe three months. But as the band progressed, they had 167 men in the band. Some could read and some couldn't read. So they said they was going to find out who could read and who couldn't read. So they sent old man Joe Martinez there to break up the band. That's what he was sent there for to break up the band. So when he came, he found so many fellas could read music. He scratched his head. He said, I've got something here I can do something with. So he weeded out all them that couldn't read. And he kept all those that could read. And when he got through Gillingham, them fellas could play anything from William Tell down, with the music or without the music. They could play as much ragtime music without the music as they could play William Tell with the music. So that made a good band. And the first music week that the government put on in the city of New Orleans, we had 57 men that came down Canal Street from Claiborne to Hell and End Station. And we played everything from Stars and Stripes Forever down to Gloria. And when we passed World Lines coming back, we hit Chicago Tribune. And you thought it was thunder when we hit Chicago Tribune.

But somehow they didn't keep the band up. They come and people get and work. And the band went down to three or four men. And I got disgusted and I left the band. And the fellow offered me more and more there to trade. And I just went on back to trade.
